correctness.rationale: The finite-Heisenberg classification identifies degree m exactly with central characters of exact order m. Orthogonal projection onto the sum of those central eigenspaces gives the Ramanujan kernel directly. Endpoint norms equal total variation of that central convolution measure. The absolute Ramanujan-period sum is proved prime-power by prime-power and multiplied by the Chinese remainder theorem. The complementary norm follows by separating the identity coefficient. Exact rational verification for \\(2\\le n\\le120\\) checks 601 divisor layers, idempotence, pairwise orthogonality, identity resolution, ranks, both norm formulas, and the contractivity criterion. The computation is corroborative; the proof is universal.

Greenleaf's older theorem covers only the abstract structure of norm-one idempotent measures, not the quantitative all-degree result. residual_risks: The full text of the 2014 Ramanujan-subspace paper was not inspected; it may contain the cyclic absolute-sum norm formula under a signal-processing normalization, although it would not by itself identify finite-Heisenberg representation-degree layers.

The exact absolute Ramanujan-sum identity is elementary and may be recorded independently in number-theoretic literature; originality is claimed for the nonabelian degree-layer theorem and its combined quantitative consequences, not for that classical arithmetic identity alone.

value.rationale: The degree strata of the regular representation are canonical spectral objects, and their endpoint projection norms are natural noncommutative Lebesgue constants. The theorem gives the complete layer decomposition for every n and every divisor degree, identifies an unexpected Ramanujan kernel on the center, and yields the exact arithmetic contractivity criterion that only powers of two survive. This is a structural all-parameter classification rather than a fixed-size computation, renaming, or arbitrary slice.
